chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from more than one of our companions from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding

The apostate is asked to repent; if he repents, he is spared, otherwise he is killed. And the woman, if she apostatizes, is asked to repent; if she repents and returns, she is spared, otherwise she is confined to prison and hardship is imposed upon her in her detention.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in punishment between a male and female apostate in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s al--Istibsar establishes the distinct jurisprudential positions of the Imams regarding apostasy, highlighting a key difference between male and female offenders. While men face execution upon refusal to repent, women are subjected to prolonged imprisonment (habs) with intensified hardship, reflecting the Shia view that their punishment is corrective rather than capital. This ruling underscores the principle of 'istitabah' (seeking repentance) as a prerequisite for the final penalty in both cases.
